A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT2 study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original supervised-training and GRPO experiments on MNNS, ProntoQA, and ProsQA, including accuracies, token entropies, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, trajectory-budget experiments, and an inference-entropy analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 introduces hindsight top-B trajectory selection: complete trajectories are ranked by a terminal score and their intermediate states form supervision targets. For MNNS, ranking uses the absolute final sum. This substantially extends v1's all-expansions supervision, while retaining its full-budget case, token-mixture loss, and GRPO procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNNS, including four- and five-input cases, and the same structured ProntoQA/ProsQA reasoning tasks. The new budget, baseline, and embedding experiments do not introduce different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 evaluates COCONUT alongside CoT2 and discrete CoT in Figure 2b and Table 3. It also adds explicit no-CoT comparisons across all three tasks; v1's final-answer-only supervision discussion concerned MNNS. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New experiments sweep B = 1, 4, 8, 16 across embedding dimensions 16, 24, 32. Appendix B.3 specifies matched total epochs for baseline comparisons and equal allocation across COCONUT curriculum stages; training with trigonometric embeddings is also newly reported. Existing splits, data representations, empirical metrics, and GRPO settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a budget-by-dimension sensitivity study testing when additional parallel trajectories help, and an inference-entropy probe testing alignment with CSFT supervision. It also briefly reports empirical validation of the trigonometric construction. The existing teacher-forcing, sparse-supervision, embedding-size, and sampling analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 specifies five-run averages for Figure 2b–c and adds shaded bands to the MNNS training curves in Figure 3, without defining the bands' statistical meaning. The ten-repeat Pass@k and Maj@k evaluations were already documented in v1; an increase in those repetitions is not reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds four-method results in Table 3, including MNNS accuracies of 98.94% for CoT2 and 92.58% for COCONUT, plus budget-sweep results and inference entropies of 0.6896, 1.3682, 1.9588, and 0.2461. It reports perfect accuracy with the trigonometric construction and changes the MNNS training curves. Existing GRPO table values remain unchanged; the additions do not establish across-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Proposition 3 changes from an L1/TV approximation guarantee with sample complexity Θ(v/(Kε²)) to an L2 guarantee Θ(1/(Kε²)), adding a squared-error comparison with factor 2−1/K and a substantially rewritten variance proof. Appendix D also introduces a robust-decoding packing argument requiring d = Ω(B log(v/B)). The underlying MNNS MoE construction remains in Appendix D.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction elevate budget-constrained CSFT and dimension-dependent optimal parallelism to central contributions, and explicitly claim superiority over alternative methods. V1 emphasized parallel reasoning and supervised-to-RL training without this budget-controlled contribution. Those original claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 now explains when smaller budgets help limited-capacity embeddings and connects that behavior to a packing bound. Appendix C.1 interprets entropy patterns as evidence of parallel search during inference. V1's warning about reduced interpretability is removed, although its embedding-capacity limitation is retained and developed elsewhere.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code repository link on the first page and adds baseline implementation details in Appendix B.3, particularly COCONUT's curriculum and epoch allocation. Existing optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, GPU, and training-time disclosures are largely unchanged. The PDFs establish the added link, not its external availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive comparisons with concurrent work by Zhu et al., Soft Thinking by Zhang et al., and hybrid latent RL by Yue et al., while removing the Snell et al. citation. The main positioning relative to COCONUT, CODI, and CCOT remains. Publication updates for Ildiz and Xiong do not represent new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten around trajectory budgets. Theory moves before reinforcement learning, related work moves from Section 1.1 to Section 6, and a conclusion replaces the former ending with limitations. Supervision and results explanations are extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn around budgets 1, 2, and 8. Figure 2 gains baseline and budget bar charts; its former training panels become Figure 3 and Appendix Figure 5, with the MNNS curves also redrawn with bands. V2 adds Table 3, reduces Table 2 to a wrapped display, and rearranges appendix figures and table captions.

improvement.justification: The COCONUT comparison, matched epoch budgets, and budget-capacity experiments improve empirical support and clarify when CSFT is useful. However, new ProntoQA accuracies are not reconciled with retained results: CoT2 scores 98.01% in Table 3 versus 75.36% before GRPO in Table 2. V2 also removes the interpretability caveat, and the revised multi-step proof does not establish its claimed variance reduction under repeated shared-mixture sampling. These shortcomings limit the net quality gain.
